author_decision.reason: Adopt ar03_trial scientific model unchanged as the final revision of ar01_initial: recurring excessive initial Spearman dependence is explained by deterministic distribution integration and addressed by a core/broad copula correlation change that preserves intended baseline covariance. Keep all marginal and regression parameters. The revision trial supports the dependence adjustment but has unfavorable E1/E2 deviations; do not compensate a single seed or claim global validation. Freeze before the three paired final deliveries.
addressed_findings: All three initial delivery Spearman correlations (.416044,.412842,.438124) exceeded supplied .361457; deterministic 48/64-node integration predicted about .426 at core rho .28.
Core/broad copula correlations change from [.28,.5871524663503118] to [.12,.6076353385661598]; all generator code, margins and covariate shifts remain unchanged from initial delivery.

Deterministic 64-node integration predicts Spearman approximately .36126 for revised dependence; isolated revision seed6201 produced .3681649, with Pearson .6613278. These are development-reference consistency findings.

The unfavorable revision-trial regressions are retained: E1=.0654375 exceeds reference interval upper .0641659, and E2=.4350492 exceeds .4329004; E3=.0087903. No equivalence inference or seed-specific correction is made.
Actual all30 feedback from every trial and all three initial deliveries, plus retained marginal/covariance/rank calculation scripts and immutable quadrature input, are hash-bound.
remaining_limitations: CHNS reference estimates and cluster-based intervals are exposed sample estimates, not population truth or independent validation.
Only three initial deliveries and one revised trial have been observed; final paired deliveries are pending at freeze, and no revision follows final results.

Regression estimates, quantiles and SDs vary with finite tail draws. The revision trial has unfavorable E1/E2 deviations; synthetic sampling variation excludes evidence, structural and transport uncertainty.

Age/BMI/female independence, absent sex biomarker effect, latent mixture membership, covariance scaffold, tail bounds and measurement rounding are assumptions; subgroup/causal/clustered analyses are unsupported.
The broad-component probability .16 is at the chosen optimization bound; the aggregate constraints do not uniquely identify a joint law or tails.
No external source-study replay or new original-study retrieval was performed; external study populations, measurement types and adjustment sets were not pooled.

inference: Seed ranges are conditional generation variation, not confidence intervals or independent clinical evidence. All 30 supplied reference statistics remain development inputs.
